Discovery by class query alone is incomplete: models the agent knows to document scuba modes (Garmin Descent Mk3, fenix 8, Huawei Watch Ultimate) did not appear on the first page, so a named-model probe follows and is recorded as agent-supplied, not shelf-discovered.

actions.purpose: Reconnaissance of how dive-capable smartwatches are listed on Amazon.de: two class queries without brand names, first search page each, up to ten product pages per query, search pages retained.
actions.question: Do class queries surface smartwatches with a scuba dive mode at all, and which of the plan's properties (GPS, heart rate, barometer, dive mode, depth rating, NFC payment, Android compatibility, display, battery) do listings state?

result.summary: 22 responses, 20 product pages, 2 search pages, no challenges. Query 1 (Smartwatch Tauchcomputer) surfaced three dive-capable smartwatches: Suunto Ocean (3 colour ASINs, 799 EUR), Suunto Nautic S (549 EUR), Garmin Descent G2 (2 colour ASINs, 588-650 EUR), beside cheap generic smartwatches and the Suunto D5 dive computer. Query 2 (Tauchcomputer Uhr GPS NFC) returned pure dive computers (Cressi, Mares) and noise; NFC in a query does not select for payment. Listings state dive mode, depth, display and GPS runtime; none of the three dive-capable smartwatches states NFC payment in its bullets, so payment and EN 13319 are read from manufacturer specifications.

actions.purpose: Proposal, not funded: a 'smartwatch' category as a task experiment -- classifier over titles and breadcrumbs (Smartwatches node; excludes bands, pure dive computers and accessories), claim keys gps, heart_rate_sensor, barometric_altimeter, scuba_dive_mode, nfc_payment, android_compatible; axes price, gps_runtime_hours (unit-ambiguous across vendors: GPS-only vs all-systems vs expedition), depth_rating_m, display_type. Needs committed cases from the three probe feeds and counterexamples (Suunto Nautic S: dive computer without optical HR; fenix E: no dive). Execution is R15's.
